assumptions: ASSUMPTION_BASE_REPRESENTATION_EXISTS: Source items have extractable base relational structure (edges, relations, attributes) that can be meaningfully abstracted.
ASSUMPTION_ALIGNMENT_TYPED: Alignment constraints are typed and machine-checkable (not free-form prose similarity).
ASSUMPTION_LGG_OPERATOR: Declared anti-unification operator LGG exists for the relational language and produces valid generalizations (not arbitrary summaries).
ASSUMPTION_FRESH_DISTRIBUTION: Fresh transfer domains are drawn from the same family distribution as development domains (no domain shift beyond declared scope).
ASSUMPTION_ABSTRACTION_COST_MONOTONE: Higher abstraction levels have non-decreasing description cost (not guaranteed monotone benefit).
ASSUMPTION_QUERY_REGISTERED: Query answers and invariants to be preserved are explicitly registered before abstraction (no post-hoc rationalization).
ASSUMPTION_HARM_BOUND_KNOWN: Harm bound for near-miss rejection is known and measurable (not undefined).
falsifier: Primary falsifier: matched one-shot abstraction parent achieves equal fresh-transfer yield (coverage, mapping fidelity) at lower description cost (fewer levels, simpler LGG). Secondary falsifiers: (1) Untyped alignment causes higher counterexample rate on fresh transfer than typed alignment; (2) Monotone scheduler (admit l+1 without preservation check) causes near-miss rejection to cross harm bound; (3) Distribution shift outside assumed scope causes fresh-transfer failure even with high development coverage.
hard_gate_obligations: OBLIGATION_TYPED_ALIGNMENT: All alignment constraints must be typed and machine-checkable (no prose similarity).
OBLIGATION_LGG_DECLARED: Anti-unification operator LGG must be declared and produce valid generalizations (not arbitrary summaries).
OBLIGATION_SCHEDULER_PRESERVATION: Abstraction level l+1 is admitted only after registered query answers/invariants are preserved or explicit losses are declared.
OBLIGATION_FRESH_TRANSFER_CHECK: Abstraction level is admitted only after held-out transfer improves or specific capability is unlocked.
OBLIGATION_HARM_BOUND_ENFORCED: Near-miss rejection rate must not cross declared harm bound at any abstraction level.
OBLIGATION_QUERY_REGISTERED: Query answers and invariants must be explicitly registered before abstraction (no post-hoc rationalization).
OBLIGATION_DESCRIPTION_COST_TRACKED: Description cost (complexity of abstracted schema) must be tracked and reported at each level.
minimal_counterexamples: COUNTEREXAMPLE_ONE_SHOT_DOMINATES: A matched one-shot abstraction parent (single-level induction) achieves equal coverage, equal fresh-transfer yield, and lower description cost than progressive multi-level abstraction.
COUNTEREXAMPLE_ALIGNMENT_UNTYPED: Alignment constraints are prose similarity (not typed checks) leading to spurious alignments that fail on fresh transfer.
COUNTEREXAMPLE_LGG_UNCONSTRAINED: LGG operator produces arbitrary summaries (not valid generalizations) leading to schemas that violate registered invariants.

COUNTEREXAMPLE_SCHEDULER_MONOTONE: Progressive scheduler admits abstraction level l+1 without checking preservation (violates monotone-good assumption), causing near-miss rejection to cross harm bound.
COUNTEREXAMPLE_FRESH_TRANSFER_FAIL: Schema achieves high coverage on development domains but fails on fresh transfer due to distribution shift outside assumed scope.
COUNTEREXAMPLE_QUERY_UNREGISTERED: Query answers/invariants are post-hoc rationalized (not registered before abstraction), inflating perceived mapping fidelity.
COUNTEREXAMPLE_HARM_BOUND_UNDEFINED: Harm bound for near-miss rejection is undefined, making scheduler admission criteria vacuous.
novelty_residual: Novelty claimed only for: (1) Progressive scheduler that explicitly trades off coverage vs abstraction cost with typed preservation constraints (not present in AlphaGeometry or one-shot abstraction parents); (2) Integration of neuro-symbolic multi-level abstraction (AlphaGeometry) with structural transfer (RAKL) and anti-unification (LGG) in a unified RAKL mechanic; (3) Hard bound on near-miss rejection and explicit fresh-transfer improvement criterion (stronger than typical out-of-distribution generalization). Delta over parents: AlphaGeometry lacks explicit fresh-transfer gating and near-miss bounds; structural transfer lacks multi-level induction; LGG lacks progressive scheduler. Permitted publication claim must be scoped to these residuals after strongest-parent differential is measured.
object_description: Progressive Relational Abstraction (PRA): construct a transferable relational schema from multiple examples via multi-level abstraction and progressive scheduler, rather than assuming a one-shot extractor can expose the full schema. For item xi, produce abstraction levels Gi(0)...Gi(L). For pair (i,j,l), construct partial alignment φ:Gi(l)↛Gj(l) subject to typed consistency constraints. Schema induction via LGG (anti-unification) over aligned examples I: K = LGG{φi(Gi)}i∈I. Track v(K) = (coverage, counterexample_rate, mapping_fidelity, description_cost, fresh_transfer_yield). Prefer high-alignability comparisons early, then increase abstraction/distance only after schema survives fresh checks. Abstraction is not monotone-good: a move l→l+1 is admitted only when registered query answers/invariants are preserved (or explicit losses declared), held-out transfer improves (or specific capability unlocked), and near-miss rejection does not cross harm bound. Output: SchemaProposal, authority floor 0.
oracle_or_lower_bound: Lower bound: one-shot abstraction parent that extracts schema in a single pass (no progressive levels) achieves same coverage and fresh-transfer yield at equal or lower cost. Oracle: optimal abstraction schedule that maximizes v(K) subject to typed constraints and harm bound (known only in synthetic settings).
permitted_publication_claim: PERMITTED_CLAIM_SCOPE: M1_PRA_v0 achieves higher fresh-transfer yield than one-shot abstraction parents at equal description cost on held-out domains within declared distribution scope, when progressive scheduler enforces typed preservation constraints and near-miss harm bounds. NO authority claimed for: (1) domains outside declared distribution family; (2) untyped alignment or arbitrary summary baselines; (3) abstraction schedules without preservation checks; (4) settings where harm bound is undefined or unmeasurable. Claim scope is limited to relational schema induction with registered queries/invariants and measurable harm bound.
qoi: Multi-level relational abstraction quality measured by: (1) Coverage: fraction of relational structure captured across abstraction levels; (2) Counterexample rate: rate of failed alignment constraints on fresh transfer; (3) Mapping fidelity: preservation of query answers and invariants across levels; (4) Description cost: complexity of abstracted schema relative to base; (5) Fresh transfer yield: successful generalization to held-out domains not seen during induction.
same_system_ablation: Ablations required on same input data: (1) ONE_SHOT: single-level abstraction without progressive scheduler; (2) UNTYPED_ALIGNMENT: prose similarity instead of typed constraints; (3) MONOTONE_SCHEDULER: admit l+1 without preservation checks; (4) NO_LGG: arbitrary summary instead of anti-unification; (5) NO_FRESH_CHECK: scheduler ignores held-out transfer improvement. Each ablation must run on identical development and fresh case sets to isolate specific mechanistic contributions.

strongest_parents.cost_equation: cost = neuro_solver_calls × solver_cost + grammar_constructions × construction_cost + proof_search_steps × search_cost
strongest_parents.justification: AlphaGeometry demonstrates multi-stage abstraction (geometry language → auxiliary constructions → proof search) with formal grammar constraints. Strongest parent for neuro-symbolic multi-level abstraction with typed language.

strongest_parents.cost_equation: cost = relation_preservation_checks × relation_cost + invariant_checks × invariant_cost + boundary_validations × boundary_cost
strongest_parents.justification: Existing RAKL structural transfer infrastructure provides typed relation/invariant preservation, role mapping, and boundary validation. Strongest in-repo parent for structural mapping.

strongest_parents.cost_equation: cost = pairwise_alignments × alignment_cost + generalization_computation × gen_cost + consistency_check × validation_cost
strongest_parents.justification: Plotkin anti-unification provides formal LGG operator for structured terms. Strongest parent for schema induction via least general generalization.

total_cost_equation: total_cost = development_induction_cost + progressive_scheduler_cost + alignment_validation_cost + fresh_transfer_evaluation_cost + description_cost + ablation_comparison_cost. Development induction cost = sum over development cases of (pairwise_alignments × alignment_cost + lgg_computation × gen_cost + consistency_check × validation_cost). Progressive scheduler cost = sum over levels of (admission_check_cost + preservation_check_cost + held_out_check_cost). Alignment validation cost = sum over alignments of (typed_constraint_check_cost). Fresh transfer evaluation cost = sum over fresh cases of (transfer_application_cost + counterexample_check_cost). Description cost = schema_complexity_metric. Ablation comparison cost = sum over ablations of same_system_run_cost.
